subject: Meteorology
title: The Hadley Cell
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Hadley Cell.

hook.text: The Hadley cell is the largest atmospheric circulation pattern—driving weather across the entire tropics.

buildup.text: Warm air rises at the ITCZ, flows poleward at high altitude, cools, and sinks at about 30° latitude.

discovery.text: The sinking air at 30° creates the subtropical high-pressure belts—home to the world's great deserts.

twist.text: The Hadley cell is expanding—its edges are shifting poleward, pushing arid zones into previously wetter regions.

climax.text: This expansion threatens water supplies for billions—Mediterranean and subtropical climates are drying out.

punchline.text: One giant circulation loop shapes rainfall for half the planet.

quiz.question: Where does sinking air in the Hadley cell create deserts?
